You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly show a frog placed inside the toilet bowl?
node.criteria: Pass if a frog is clearly visible within the toilet bowl; fail if the image clearly shows no frog inside the bowl; unknown if the bowl or its contents are obscured or the evidence is otherwise insufficient to determine this.
node.binding: The frog must be inside the toilet bowl of the toilet in the input image.

node_traces.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The edited image visibly shows a frog within the toilet bowl, so the trace’s “yes” is supported by the image; the reference “partial” label alone does not establish that this node is wrong. Do not tune the criterion to force partial or treat the extra frogs on the lid and floor as evidence against completion. The actionable concern is robustness: the completion trace asserts the decisive spatial relation at 0.99 confidence without explaining how it distinguishes a frog inside the bowl from one merely overlapping the rim or appearing on the lid. Refine the completion check to cite the frog’s position relative to the bowl interior and use unknown when that relation is visually ambiguous; keep partial-progress evidence separate and only relevant when completion is not established. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated: both supports were queried and passed.
s2: The binding is too broad: “progress” includes a frog clearly inside the bowl, so this support can pass on completion and blur the distinction between partial and complete fulfillment. Make the criterion explicitly test only incomplete progress (for example, a frog visibly approaching or partly entering the bowl but not yet inside); treat a clearly interior frog as not partial evidence, leaving completion to the completion check. In this image, one frog is visibly within the bowl interior, while others are on the lid and floor; the latter are unrelated to the requested placement. Require evidence to distinguish the bowl interior from the rim/lid, and return unknown if that spatial relation is ambiguous rather than asserting it with unwarranted confidence. Do not force the aggregate reference label: it does not establish atomic ground truth. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is incomplete and ambiguous: it trails off at “inside (...)” and does not clearly distinguish the bowl interior from the toilet lid, rim, or nearby surfaces. Repair the typed binding so it anchors the requested frog placement to the bowl interior and supports a completion check that requires visible evidence of that spatial relation; use unknown when overlap or occlusion makes placement unclear. In the edited image, one frog appears within the bowl, while others are on the raised lid and floor. Those extra frogs neither negate the requested placement nor establish partial fulfillment. Keep this support focused on the requested placement rather than broad “progress,” and do not alter it merely to force the aggregate “partial” label: that label is not atomic ground truth. The trace reports a pass with high confidence, so investigate whether its evidence actually distinguishes the bowl interior from the rim; low confidence or variation alone would not show the edit is absent. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
